title: Maps from a perfect complex vanish against a bounded quasi-coherent gap
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let K be a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. Then there exist integers a <= b such that for every L in D_QCoh(\mathcal O_X) whose cohomology sheaves H^i(L) vanish for all i in [a,b], one has Hom_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(K,L)=0.

proof.text: By the perfect tensor-Hom comparison [lem-pc-perfect-rhom-tensor-comparison], the dual K^\vee is perfect and has a finite Tor-amplitude interval [u,v]. The comparison identifies K^\vee\otimes^L L with R\mathcal Hom(K,L), and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] identifies H^0(X,R\mathcal Hom(K,L)) with Hom_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(K,L).

source.place: Tag 09M4 proof, lines identifying Hom(K,L) with H^0(X,K^vee tensor^L L) and choosing the Tor-amplitude interval

proof.text: Apply the hypercohomology spectral-sequence gap statement [lem-sc-perfect-hypercohomology-gap] to P=K^\vee. If H^q(L)=0 for q in [j-v,j-u], then H^j(K^\vee\otimes^L L)=0; in particular, for j=-N,...,0 it is enough that H^i(L)=0 for every i in [-v-N,-u].

source.place: Tag 09M4 proof, spectral sequence and the subsequent choice of the interval [-b-N,-a]

proof.text: Take f:X\to \operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z). Since X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and its base is affine. Clause (1) of [lem-pc-finite-support-hi] makes R^qf_*G quasi-coherent for every quasi-coherent G. Thus [lem-pc-affine-vanishing] gives H^p(\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z),R^qf_*G)=0 for p>0. The edge-map assertion [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections] then identifies H^q(X,G) with \Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z),R^qf_*G). Clause (2) of [lem-pc-finite-support-hi] supplies n with R^qf_*G=0 for q>=n; put N=\max(n,0), so H^q(X,G)=0 for every quasi-coherent G and q>=N. Let E=K^\vee\otimes^L L; it lies in D_QCoh(\mathcal O_X) (Tag 09M4: tensor of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology, a perfect complex having quasi-coherent cohomology), and assume H^i(E)=0 for -N<=i<=0. Consider the standard truncation triangle \tau_{\le -N-1}E\to E\to\tau_{\ge -N}E\to [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] and the exact sequence H^0(X,\tau_{\le -N-1}E)\to H^0(X,E)\to H^0(X,\tau_{\ge -N}E). The global sections functor \Gamma(X,-)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_X,-) commutes with products and its derived functors on quasi-coherent modules vanish in degrees >=N, so [lem-pc-unbounded-derived-functor-cohomological-bound] with b=-N-1 gives H^i(X,\tau_{\le -N-1}E)=0 for i>-2, in particular for i=0. By the assumed vanishing, \tau_{\ge -N}E\cong\tau_{\ge 1}E is bounded below with cohomology only in degrees >=1, so [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] (applied to \Gamma(X,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}) gives H^0(X,\tau_{\ge -N}E)=0. Hence H^0(X,E)=0.

source.place: Tag 09M4 proof, invocation of Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 30.4.4, Lemma 36.3.5 (Tag 08D4) and Derived Categories Lemma 13.16.1

proof.text: Set a=-v-N and b=-u. Then a<=b, and for every L whose H^i(L) vanish for i in [a,b], Step 2 makes H^j(K^\vee\otimes^L L)=0 for j=-N,...,0, while Step 3 gives H^0(X,K^\vee\otimes^L L)=0. The identification in Step 1 therefore gives Hom_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(K,L)=0.

split_report.summary: Split Stacks Tag 09M4 into the perfect-dual hypercohomology gap; the qcqs cohomology bound is supplied by existing finite-support, affine-acyclicity, and Leray nodes. The item proof identifies Hom from K with global H^0 of K-dual tensor L, applies the spectral-sequence gap over the interval [-v-N,-u], and uses the cohomological bound plus truncation to force H^0 to vanish.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the proper-flat support proof clause of lem-sc-finite-duality: choose the truncation index sufficiently negative so the extension class into the bounded quasi-coherent tail vanishes.

tool_uses.why: The final identification of derived global H^0 of the internal Hom with the Hom set in D(O_X) is a generic site-level tool, not supplied by this Picard-duality route.
The spectral-sequence proof needs the generic qcqs uniform higher-direct-image bound; this unit has no replacement for that cohomological-dimension tool.
The generic Leray edge-map isomorphism converts the quasi-coherent higher-direct-image bound on the affine base into global cohomology vanishing for the qcqs morphism X to Spec(Z).
Generic left-exact-functor fact: the right derived functor of Gamma(X,-) kills degree 0 on a bounded-below complex concentrated in degrees >=1 (Stacks 05TC).

lean.statement: theorem exists_subsingleton_hom_of_isPerfect (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] (K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hK : IsPerfect X K) : ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∀ L : schemeDerivedCategory X, schemeDerivedQCohProperty X L → (∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → i ≤ b → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) i).obj L)) → Subsingleton (K ⟶ L)

reviewed_lean.note: qcqs as [CompactSpace X][QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (as PerfectObjectCompact); K : schemeDerivedCategory X with IsPerfect X K and its HasDerivedCategory binders only; ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b before ∀ L (a,b independent of L); L in D_QCoh via schemeDerivedQCohProperty, no boundedness; H^i(L) zero via IsZero of homologyFunctor object (a sheaf, not a Type) for i in closed [a,b]; Hom(K,L)=0 as Subsingleton (K ⟶ L); node diff only adds lean; no new defs/nodes
